name: Nasrid portico
_about: A NASRID PORTICO (the Alhambra, 14th c.): N arches `bay` apart along x, centred, the arcade's middle on z 0 and the gallery behind it, `d` deep toward -z (the wall at -d is the building's). Columns of the `nasrid` order `colH` to the top of their cubic capitals -- `pairs` yes sets two on every pier, `pairGap` apart -- carrying a wall `t` thick and up to `H` in which the arches are cut, stilted: their jambs `spr` straight up from the capitals, `pierW` apart, under heads of any profile (`head` semicircular, or lobed with `lobes`; `over` a horseshoe's). A wooden ceiling, the eave `eave` out on the court side, and (`roof` yes) a shed roof of tiles `pitch` degrees over it all, high against the back wall.

columns._about: the slender marble columns, ringed at the neck, under their cubic capitals

columns a._about: or a pair on every pier (the Court of the Lions' corners and pavilions)

arcade._about: the wall the columns carry, the arches cut in it -- stilted, their jambs running straight up from the capitals -- and over them the SEBKA, the net of lozenges in plaster (the finish's)

ceiling._about: the gallery's wooden ceiling, from the arcade back to the wall behind

eave._about: the carved wooden eave on its brackets, far out over the arcade

roof._about: a roof of tiles falling to the eave (`roof` no: the building roofs it)
